subject: science
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Science changes with evidence
outcomes: Learner can explain with an example how scientific ideas change when new evidence appears
misconceptions: Thinks scientific knowledge is fixed and never changes
hooks: From "Earth is flat" to satellite photos; ISRO missions

topics.title: Science as a shared human effort
outcomes: Learner can describe how people across cultures and times, including Indian scientists, built scientific knowledge
misconceptions: Thinks science is done only by famous people in laboratories abroad
hooks: C.V. Raman wondering why the sea is blue

chapters.title: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral

topics.title: Natural indicators
outcomes: Learner can use litmus, turmeric and red rose/hibiscus extracts to classify substances as acidic, basic or neutral
misconceptions: Thinks all acids are dangerous and burn the skin
Believes a substance that tastes sour is the only kind of acid
hooks: Haldi stain turns red with soap

topics.title: Neutralisation in daily life
outcomes: Learner can explain neutralisation and its everyday uses
misconceptions: Believes mixing an acid and a base always produces something harmful
hooks: Antacid for acidity; lime for acidic soil; baking soda on an ant bite

topics.title: Cells, bulbs and closed circuits
outcomes: Learner can build a simple circuit and explain why the bulb glows only when the circuit is closed
misconceptions: Thinks one wire from the cell to the bulb is enough
Believes the bulb uses up current so less returns to the cell
hooks: How a torch works: open one up

topics.title: Circuit diagrams and switches
outcomes: Learner can draw circuit diagrams using standard symbols and use a switch
misconceptions: Thinks a switch "makes" electricity
hooks: The switchboard in your room

topics.title: Conductors and insulators
outcomes: Learner can test materials and classify them as conductors or insulators
misconceptions: Believes water and the human body never conduct electricity
hooks: Why electricians wear rubber gloves

chapters.title: The World of Metals and Non-metals

topics.title: Properties of metals and non-metals
outcomes: Learner can compare metals and non-metals for malleability, ductility, sonority and conduction
misconceptions: Thinks all metals are hard solids (ignores mercury, sodium)
hooks: Temple bells ring; copper wires; silver varq on sweets

topics.title: Effect of air and water on metals
outcomes: Learner can describe rusting of iron and how it can be prevented
misconceptions: Believes rust is just dirt on iron
hooks: A cycle left outside in the monsoon

topics.title: Uses of non-metals
outcomes: Learner can explain why non-metals like oxygen, carbon and nitrogen are essential
misconceptions: Thinks non-metals are not useful
hooks: Oxygen cylinders in hospitals; graphite in pencils

chapters.title: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical

topics.title: Physical and chemical changes
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
misconceptions: Believes all changes can be reversed
Thinks melting ice is a chemical change because it looks different
hooks: Melting ghee vs burning a diya wick

topics.title: Rusting and combustion
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
misconceptions: Thinks burning destroys matter completely
hooks: Why is a sigri fanned to keep it burning?

topics.title: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
misconceptions: Believes rocks never change
hooks: Rounded pebbles in a mountain stream

chapters.title: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change

topics.title: Changes during adolescence
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
misconceptions: Thinks everyone goes through changes at exactly the same age
hooks: Height chart on the wall over the years

topics.title: Emotional changes and seeking help
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
misconceptions: Believes it is wrong or shameful to talk about these changes
hooks: A question box in class for anonymous questions

topics.title: Nutrition, hygiene and activity
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
misconceptions: Thinks skipping meals helps one stay fit
hooks: Iron-rich foods like spinach, jaggery and chana

topics.title: Conduction
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
misconceptions: Believes woollen clothes produce heat
Thinks metals feel cold because they are colder
hooks: Steel spoon in hot chai gets hot; wooden ladle does not

topics.title: Convection, land and sea breeze
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
misconceptions: Thinks heat only moves upward
hooks: Sea breeze at Marina beach in the afternoon

topics.title: Radiation
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
misconceptions: Believes heat cannot travel through empty space
hooks: Dark vs white cloth in the sun

topics.title: The water cycle and groundwater
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
misconceptions: Thinks underground water is a big lake
hooks: Why borewells go dry in summer

topics.title: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
misconceptions: Thinks a heavier bob makes the pendulum swing faster
hooks: Sundials at Jantar Mantar; a swing in the park

topics.title: Speed
outcomes: Learner can calculate speed from distance and time and compare speeds
misconceptions: Thinks the vehicle that travels farther is always faster
Confuses speed with distance
hooks: Speed of a Vande Bharat vs a passenger train

topics.title: Uniform and non-uniform motion
outcomes: Learner can distinguish uniform and non-uniform motion from data
misconceptions: Believes motion is uniform whenever an object keeps moving
hooks: An auto in city traffic vs a train on a straight track

topics.title: Digestion in humans
outcomes: Learner can describe the path of food through the digestive system and what happens at each stage
misconceptions: Thinks food goes straight from the mouth to the stomach unchanged
Believes the stomach is where all digestion happens
hooks: Why chewing a roti for long makes it taste sweet

topics.title: Nutrition in other animals
outcomes: Learner can compare how different animals take in and digest food
misconceptions: Believes all animals digest food the same way as humans
hooks: Why a cow chews cud

topics.title: Respiration in animals
outcomes: Learner can explain breathing and respiration and how different animals breathe
misconceptions: Thinks breathing and respiration are the same thing
Believes we breathe in only oxygen and breathe out only carbon dioxide
hooks: Count breaths per minute after running

topics.title: Photosynthesis
outcomes: Learner can explain that plants make food in leaves using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
misconceptions: Believes plants get their food from the soil
Thinks plants do not respire, or respire only at night
hooks: Starch test on a leaf kept partly covered

topics.title: Exchange of gases through stomata
outcomes: Learner can describe stomata and gas exchange in leaves
misconceptions: Thinks plants take in only carbon dioxide and never oxygen
hooks: Peel of a leaf under a magnifier

topics.title: Transport of water and food in plants
outcomes: Learner can explain how water and minerals move up and food moves to all parts
misconceptions: Believes water moves down from leaves to roots
hooks: White flowers turning colour in dyed water

topics.title: Sources of light and materials
outcomes: Learner can classify sources as luminous or non-luminous and materials as transparent, translucent or opaque
misconceptions: Thinks the Moon is a source of light
hooks: Butter paper vs glass vs cardboard against a torch

topics.title: Shadow formation
outcomes: Learner can explain how shadows form because light travels in straight lines
misconceptions: Believes shadows are reflections of the object
Thinks a shadow shows the colour of the object
hooks: Shadow puppets on a wall

topics.title: Reflection and plane mirrors
outcomes: Learner can describe reflection and images in a plane mirror (lateral inversion)
misconceptions: Thinks the image is on the surface of the mirror
hooks: AMBULANCE written in reverse

topics.title: Pinhole camera, periscope and kaleidoscope
outcomes: Learner can make a pinhole camera or periscope and explain how it works
misconceptions: Believes the image in a pinhole camera is upright
hooks: View a bulb through a pinhole camera

topics.title: Rotation and revolution of the Earth
outcomes: Learner can explain day-night by rotation and the year by revolution
misconceptions: Thinks the Sun moves around the Earth each day
hooks: Why the Sun rises earlier in Arunachal than in Gujarat

topics.title: Seasons
outcomes: Learner can explain seasons by the tilt of the Earth’s axis
misconceptions: Believes seasons happen because the Earth is closer to the Sun in summer
hooks: Why it is winter in Australia when it is summer in India

topics.title: Solar and lunar eclipses
outcomes: Learner can explain how solar and lunar eclipses occur and how to view them safely
misconceptions: Thinks eclipses happen every new moon and full moon
Believes the phases of the Moon are caused by the Earth’s shadow
hooks: Safe solar viewing with a pinhole
